fixes.explanation: Yes, sitting. John 20:12 says the two angels in white were sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet. Sitting in that spot is quiet, and nothing in the verse says they were doing anything else.

That's right. Jesus tells her to go and tell His brothers, "I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God." (John 20:17). He's giving her a message to carry to them. She's the one trusted to deliver it.

That's what Mary sees, and it's the first thing that tells her something is off. She gets there while it's still dark, and the stone is no longer at the entrance (John 20:1). Imagine walking up to your own front door in the dark and the door is just GONE. Friend, I think she stopped dead in her tracks.

Cracked would be a dramatic detail, but the text never says it. John 20:1 says she saw that the stone had been "…removed from the entrance." Removed, not cracked, not smashed. The entrance is open when she arrives.

Not quite, friend. Mary says the opposite. She tells them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have put Him!" (John 20:2). So she has no idea where the body is, and she comes running to Peter and the other disciple with that news.

Right, because Mary doesn't know at all. She says, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have put Him!" (John 20:2). She's missing the answer, and she runs to tell Peter and the other disciple anyway. Ever sprint to tell somebody a problem you can't solve yet? That's Mary.

Yes, the head. John 20:7 says the cloth that had been around Jesus' head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths. It's a small detail, but the writer thought it was worth including. I think Peter noticed that cloth sitting off by itself.

Moses and Elijah do appear in another Bible scene, on the mountain with Jesus (Matthew 17:3). But that's a different moment from this one. Here Mary sees two angels in white (John 20:12). They're sitting where the body of Jesus had lain.

Yes, the gardener. John 20:15 says she was "Thinking He was the gardener…" So she asks Him where the body has been put. She doesn't recognize Him yet (John 20:14), and a man standing there is who she takes Him to be.

Peace is a good guess, but it isn't the word here. With Mary, Jesus says one word, and it's her name: "Mary" (John 20:16). That's the moment she turns and says, "Rabboni!" It's a name, not a greeting.

That's what she was looking for earlier, when she asked the one she thought was the gardener where they had put Him (John 20:15). But her announcement in John 20:18 is, "I have seen the Lord!" She saw Him, and that's what she tells the disciples.
